data.cultural_impact: The name Pranab in Hindu context is associated with the renouncer and philosopher Paranandasar Maharaj (1530-1606 AD), also known as Pran sample Prabhu or Sidhesvar Swami, who was regarded as the 10th guru of the Nath tradition. The term 'Prana' meaning life-force is deeply embedded in Hindu culture and beliefs, and the name Pranab signifies a person who embodies and nurtures this vital energy of life.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Pranab represents a divine being who is the embodiment of Prana (life-force or breath) and as such, he is perceived as the giver and sustainer of life. The spiritual seeker aspires to attain such a state where they too can nurture life-force within themselves and in others, ultimately leading to spiritual enlightenment. The name is also a reminder to value and cherish the precious gift of life.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Anita Pranab in Delhi, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Pranab, which means "Prana (life) + Ab (father)". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Pranab: The embodiment of nurturing and giving life, symbolized by the gentle flow of prana (life force) within.
